newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon says backlog $23 bln with new units.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon says backlog $23 bln with new units.

text.p: Raytheon Corp said its backlog will be about $23 billion including its acquisitions of Hughes Electronics defense operations and Texas Instruments' defense operations.
Of the $23 billion, defense electronics will account for about $18 billion, the company said.
The company's total backlog at the end of 1996, excluding the acquisitions, totaled $12.1 billion, up $1.5 billion -- or 14.4 percent -- from the end of 1995.
The company agreed to pay $2.95 billion in cash for Texas Instruments operations and $5.1 billion in common stock and $4.4 billion in debt for Hughes.
Officials from Raytheon could not be reached to comment.
Raytheon said the two transactions are scheduled to close by mid-year.

They are still subject to regulatory approvals, the company added. The Hughes transaction is still subject to a favorable ruling from the International Revenue Service and and approval by both Raytheon's and General Motors Corp's stockholders.

Later in the day, a Raytheon spokesman said "timing delays" in closing several international contracts won by the company's Engineers & Constructors unit were primarily behind the earnings shortfall for the quarter, compared with the year-earlier period.

"Resolving some financing elements was the cause of the delays," said Bob McWade, the Raytheon spokesman. He said there were less than a dozen contracts, although he would not specify the number of contracts or how much the contracts were worth. He said one of the contracts was in Indonesia.
McWade said that Raytheon had already won the contracts and was "confident" it would close them soon -- some as early as the first quarter.
The company also said that its Massachusetts-based defense operations experienced declines in sales and income.
McWade said the declines resulted from lower U.S. defense expenditures.
He said the company "sees an improving picture there (at the Massachusetts defense operations) this year."
Analysts surveyed by First Call had expected Raytheon to report fourth-quarter earnings of $0.75 per share and earnings of $3.30 per share for the 1996 full year.
